verdict.tagline: Fast combat and deep progression keep every descent fresh despite repeating early floors.
for_you_if: you enjoy fast and fluid action combat
you want rich dialogue that evolves across runs
you appreciate deep weapon and boon combinations
not_for_you_if: you dislike repeating early stages after dying
you find repetitive gameplay loops tedious

single_points.text: One reviewer says it came to Steam later after being an Epic exclusive.

citation.review_text:
Former Epic exclusive. When it comes to mobile, it was released as an iOS exclusive, and available exclusively through Netflix. Due to the nature of subscription based services, it has only been available that way for about one year, until it was removed, and it's currently unavailable anywhere outside of PC and consoles. Obviously when it comes to PC it came to Steam later, after they took the Epic bribe money.

They sure are willing to screw their customers if the bribe is high enough.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the artstyle and soundtrack are beautiful.

citation.review_text: Only game worthy enough to make me buy it on two platforms so i guess that says more than enough. Beautiful artstyle and beautiful soundtrack. Overall chef's kiss.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the upgrade process is lengthy, tedious, and time-consuming.

citation.review_text:
Maybe we're talking about the real GOTY of 2020.

Honestly, I'm not particularly into Hades, but even I can appreciate what Supergiant Games has accomplished here. A masterpiece of the roguelite genre, seasoned with some good old family drama and humor.

An addictive, almost perfectly crafted gameplay loop, with Megaera and the music being, without a doubt, the highlights of the experience.

Of course, the game isn't without its flaws: the lengthy, tedious, and time-consuming upgrade process, the skin tones of Athena and Ares, and issues with certain boss fights.

9.5/10

cohorts.summary: Players praise the fast combat and smooth handheld performance, though some find the constant restarts and early stages repetitive over time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as fast-paced, fluid, and engaging.

citations.review_text: The combat and gameplay in Hades are top-notch fast paced and engaging making it easy to get hooked on the game. However the protagonist's emotional baggage starts to feel like a chore after a few runs.
This game is very fun and fast paces.
love the Art-Style, fluid gameplay, interesting lore, unique mechanics (Beside beeing roguelite). i can see myself investing a large ammount of hours into this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that dying and restarting runs sends the player back to the beginning repeatedly.

citations.review_text:
The game is no good.
I´ve had fun for the first 3 or 4 runs i played it which maybe were 2 hours tops after which the game gets insanely repetitive and just boring.

For a game that focuses on gameplay and replayability it´s sad to say that it fails on both fronts.
The gameplay is okay, it´s average, nothing special.
My biggest problem is that every time i got stuck on a boss fight or particularly difficult room i had to restart the whole run.´
In theory this is fine and roguelikes are meant to be played this way but in Hades its just so anoying to have to play through these first stages over and over again, everytime the exact same thing.
I´ve played games where this worked out totally fine but for me Hades just does this very bad.
And if i´ve wanted to unlock every small little, even just cosmetic, thing in the game, or unlock all the dialogs for all the characters the ingame economy really just screws with me.
After 2 hours i started loosing fun and after beating the game a few times and a total of 12 hours i only unlocked a fraction of the optional content and there is just no motivation, no fun, to continue to play this game for any reason.

As a roguelike this game stinks, allthough i heard the sequal is supposed to be a lot better.
Fun rogue like , go in die come back try again , can get repetitive but it’s def worth on sale

citations.review_text:
Yeah. I'm here to say what every other negative rating has said already. Fun at first, then the repetitiveness get tedious. Too much grind and it's not rewarding. You don't feel the grow or that you're getting stronger and unlocking more and more; at least it's not felt enough to make starting from the very beginning each time worth it.

Maybe it's not objectively bad, it's just not for everyone, but it is absolutely overrated.

In theory this is fine and roguelikes are meant to be played this way but in Hades its just so anoying to have to play through these first stages over and over again, everytime the exact same thing.

After 2 hours i started loosing fun and after beating the game a few times and a total of 12 hours i only unlocked a fraction of the optional content and there is just no motivation, no fun, to continue to play this game for any reason.

As a roguelike this game stinks, allthough i heard the sequal is supposed to be a lot better.

An okay game. The gameplay loop is not that interesting after a while, there's simply not too much content so you end up repeating same stuff over and over and it gets boring. Meanwhile the upgrade system is way too complex for it's own good. You need to figure out the mirror, the keepsakes, the boons, the hammers, poms, the weapons aspects etc in order to create a decent build and most of it is "try this new thing, oh no, it sucks, let's remember that it sucks and don't pick that up ever again". Many, many upgrades just barely do anything, it honestly felt like slamming your head into the wall and brute forcing it in order to clear one escape attempt in about 20 runs. And the game suggests to do that again multiple times, no thanks. Especially considering that it's very RNG based so you end up not finding good upgrades. In short, this game while not being inherently bad, was not that enjoyable for me, and honestly made me appreciate the other rogue-likes I played even more.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players highlight the extensive dialogue, varied combinations, smooth performance on older hardware, and the rewarding difficulty progression with advanced modifiers.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the difficulty progression as challenging initially but balancing out as players improve, with the Pact of Punishment / Heat system adding further mechanics and difficulty modifiers after completing standard runs.

citations.review_text: Revisited this masterpiece on it's anniversary. What a beautiful piece of art Supergiant have made. Art style is impeccable, music perfectly fits the atmosphere and gameplay never gets old. Strange that the difficulty is perfectly balanced. I remember getting my balls kicked in by the game at the start and slowly getting better, Zagreus getting stronger accordingly and the games progression not even slightly getting stalled after finishing runs multiple times. The pact that regulates the difficulty and actually adds gameplay mechanics after completing the game on normal difficulties never let's the gameplay get stale. A masterclass at interesting gameplay solutions.

Again thanking that generous guy, u/Aggravating_Chest410 , who gifted me this game.

Finished it for like the 3rd time, First playthrough was on 2020-21 prolly, only beat 'Dad' once, then thought its finished.
Got up to it in 2024, and then I become really hooked on it, spent 70+ hours, off steam, just to see the credits roll. Got deep into greek myth, wouldn't happen tho, if zeus just kept his zipper closed.
these two playthrough was on Mouse/Keeb, got so better at playing that I could beat 'Dad' with eyes closed, it became a peak muscle memory.

Then in 2026, 3 days before finals, got this as a gift, and heard that credits aint the end of the game, so said fk u to exams, and started grinding for 10 straight days.
This time beat hades only in 3 run, and finished and 100%ed the game with 89 runs.

Yet this game never disappoints, still loading it up today to play and figure out that there's still stories, hearts, pacts to be fulfilled. AND the HEAT 💀

Its one of my favourite games, that I'll recommend to everyone, just not for the peak combat and artworks, as it has another level of bgm that makes every fight, every run worth it.

"I'll sleep when I'm Dead"

and fuck you filthy rats (Vermin & Satyr)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive dialogue and a wide variety of weapon and boon combinations that keep individual runs feeling fresh and unique.

citations.review_text: I resumed this game after having a playtime of 12hrs just to clear my library and stop purchasing extra games unneccasarily, even though I was hesitant to do so. Best decision ever. I only sort of completed it and what an amazing experience it was. So much lore, so many dialogues (like seriously how tf do they have so many dialogues???). Even though I was frustrated with the game initially (this was my first roguelike), it slowly grew on me. 9.5/10. It's extremely fun to experiment on different weapons with different boons and majority of the runs never feel the same because of it.

Absolutely fantastic game! The gameplay is addictive, the combat feels amazing, and the art style and soundtrack are just beautiful. The characters are incredibly well-written, and the dialogue makes every run feel fresh and interesting. It's one of those games where you keep telling yourself "just one more run." Definitely a must-play!

got this game more then 4 years ago, never finished it, i jast get back to it every couple of months. the game play is so fun and smove even on my old potato laptop. even tho i couldent get past the first third for a long time, the game its so fun and replayable its is still incredable. great game and a great story on top of all. really love it<3

single_points.text: One reviewer says your hand gets tired from constantly mashing buttons, and wrists would still hurt the following day.

citation.review_text:
(+) Excellent replayability. You can keep coming back to this game over and over again.

(+) It's worth farming resources early on to upgrade your character rather than immediately trying to beat the game. This makes progression more engaging and adds to the replayability.

(+) The game offers a decent level of difficulty while remaining fair. So far, I haven't noticed any situations where the game takes away your HP unfairly. (After 80 hours, I can say that the game is actually extremely easy.)

(+) I really liked the visuals.

(+) The soundtrack is absolutely top-tier for this genre.

(-) Your hand gets tired from constantly mashing buttons. You can't play for that long without feeling it. This is a major downside, as my wrists would still hurt the following day. After a few days of playing, though, my hands eventually got used to it.

(-) Over time, running through the same biomes over and over again just to reach the final boss gets boring. A single run takes around 25–35 minutes, and dying along the way is extremely unlikely. The only real chance of dying is at the final boss, and even then, usually only if you get an unlucky set of abilities. Eventually, the repetition starts to wear thin.

(-) There's too much downtime between runs. You have to go around talking to all the NPCs and visit your room before you can start another run. In a roguelike, I want to be able to jump into the next attempt as quickly as possible.

(+/-) A lot of variety in terms of weapons, abilities, and rooms to choose from. Although the more I played, the more I realized that the actual variety isn't quite as extensive as it initially seems.

(+/-) I enjoyed the constant dialogue with gods and demigods. However, the more I played, the more repetitive and annoying these conversations became.

(+/-) Some achievements simply aren't worth going for. They just waste your time without offering anything new or particularly satisfying in return. There's no real challenge or sense of accomplish…

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players emphasize the consistently smooth and responsive combat controls.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat controls as smooth, responsive, and tactile.

citations.review_text: I don't think I've played any real-time game with a more satisfying feel than this one. It's just so smooth and responsive. The way the character and the player grow slightly stronger together with each run (successful or failed) is beautifully balanced. The art style is stunning. The music (both the non-diegetic as well as the songs being sung in game) is unbelievably pleasing. Delightful characters, an insane amount of recorded dialogue that feels responsive to your actions, and a really well done story. An easy 10/10.

The sounds and input response are the most rewarding aspects of this game. I like the story and it compels you to keep trying, but it really is the tactile response that keeps me coming back for more!

single_points.text: One reviewer says Hades does a great job of incrementally unlocking lore, weapons, and weapon modifications called Boons while you develop relationships and cross milestones.

citation.review_text:
Not a ton to say. If you like these types of games, you'll love Hades. End of. And the lore is really fun to unlock bit by bit as you develop your relationships and cross milestones with the characters. Hades does a great job of incrementally unlocking lore, weapons, modifications to those weapons (called Boons), and keeping you engaged long after most Roguelikes would start to feel stale. 100h into the game feels like basically nothing because it's still enjoyable.

If you *don't* like chasing endgame/postgame content, you'll still get your money's worth just beating it until the "end," but there is plenty to unlock afterward.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game stops the timer when you meet a character playing music so you can stop and admire the song.

citation.review_text:
You know, there are many nice things about this game. 

But I will tell you my favourite. 

In a game where time matters, there is a part where, sometimes, you meet a character playing music. And I really like the song.

The game stops the timer, in that part, in case you want to just stop and admire the song.

Which I did. May times. Good riddance.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that to reach the true ending you must beat the final boss 10 times, and to get the epilogue ending you must have specific high heart relationships with the Olympian gods.

citation.review_text: just straight peak. addictive roguelike elements, with satisfying combat, and the characters are unique and fun with great personality put into the voice acting. in order to reach the true ending you must beat the final boss 10 times, but in order to get the epilogue ending you must have a 7 heart relationship all olympian gods but Hermes must be 8 hearts and Demeter 6 hearts.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game offers a God Mode if the learning curve feels too steep.

citation.review_text:
By the 100-hour mark, I have successfully reached the epilogue and completed most of the NPC questlines. I am now going for 100% achievements. This is one of the first games I have ever purchased on Steam. Supergiant did a great job with the music and voice acting, especially their portrayal of Hades and the love he has for his wife.

I love the core roguelike mechanics, where each run feels unique and different boon combinations lead to completely different outcomes. Even after 100 hours, there are still many things I haven't tried, such as the other weapons. I finished the main story and epilogue using only the sword, so I am excited to explore the rest of the arsenal. The Heat system keeps the game addictive long after unlocking the main achievements, making it a game with endless replay value.

My personal favorite characters are Artemis, Nyx, and Dionysus. They are always a highlight whenever I encounter them during a run.

The world design across the different regions (Tartarus, Asphodel, Elysium, Greece, and the Temple of Styx) is distinct and visually striking. Seeing Greece for the first time after defeating the final boss was picturesque.

The main boss fight in Elysium was a bit frustrating on initial runs, but it eventually became fun. On the other hand, the main boss of Asphodel felt a bit too easy, even on my first playthrough.

While the game offers a God Mode if the learning curve feels too steep, I recommend experiencing it on the default difficulty.

As for characters I did not connect with as much, Ares stands out. I usually avoid his boons and pick other options instead.

I completed my first five successful runs using a keyboard and mouse, but I switched to a controller after getting one. The story progression feels smooth, making it easy to play for 2 to 3 hours in a single session. It is one of the few games where I do not even keep background yt videos or podcasts playing while I play.

I have not bought the sequel yet, as I want to get 100% …

single_points.text: One reviewer says the way you progress quests is by talking to each character once after each run to exhaust all their possible dialogue until they finally talk about their quest.

citation.review_text: Amazing soundtrack, fantastic smooth gameplay, lovely writing and characters. However, i'd say this game is more of a story game than a proper roguelite. The game is really fun i just don't think it has the same replayability as other games. It's like you progress through a lovely story by playing through what is essentially the same game over and over again. Your build and weapons will be different but the enemies and levels aren't. I decided to 100% the game and it was very fun right up until the last push and it honestly became a a bit of a slog. The way you progress quests is you just talk to characters and you can talk to each character 1 time after each run and in order to progress quests you basically have to talk to them to exhaust all their possible to dialogue until they finally talk about their quest in which you just continue playing the game the same way and talking to them until it eventually resolves. Honestly i found the game quite difficult at the start and struggled quite a bit to get my first win but honestly after that and the more you play you just get too good at it and it just becomes kind of boring as theres little challenge and little incentive to win either. my longest win streak was like 32 before i just started dying at the start of runs to cycle dialogue faster to just get the last few quests done. i mean i even won a run completely hitless start to finish and im not particularly good at games so i think that speaks to the difficulty lol. Anyway ive heard they improved the quest system in the next game so i look forward to playing that eventually. All in all, i think this is a really good game, id give it like a 9/10. I just wouldn't reccomend playing it past like the resolution of the main story.
